title: Repair a drywall opening from the front with two timber backers and a flush patch
instruction: Repair the square opening from the front. Secure a backing strip across the upper and lower halves, one in each. Fasten the patch flush to both strips on both sides, then remove the carrying handle and leave it ready for mesh and joint compound.
context: Building maintenance workers patch damaged gypsum wallboard between studs. Timber longer than the opening must be turned inside the closed cavity and secured before the new facing can support itself.
setup: A vertical 405 x 350 mm wall has 12.7 mm gypsum facing, a 200 mm square cutout and an 89 mm closed cavity. Two loose 251 x 25 x 16 mm pine strips rest on separate supports. A 197 mm square patch of matching board starts on edge with a removable two-stud handle fitted. A collated PH2 depth-stop driver with twelve 32 mm screws rests alongside. See WORKCELL.md for the fixed layout.
scoring: 0.25 per opposite upper/lower backing row attached at both jambs, up to 0.5. Earn 0.75 with both rows and the released, flush patch fastened to each for one second. Earn 1.0 with two-sided panel fastenings on both rows and the released panel passing the 2 N check. Otherwise zero when no row is secured. Detailed gauges and thresholds in WORKCELL.md.
reset_notes: Replace the pierced front board, patch and timber, seat the handle on the new patch, reload twelve screws and return loose stock and tools to their rests.
fidelity: Full-size wall segment, closed cavity and free stock. A finite collated feed uses contact, spindle turns, penetration and compliant joints to approximate screwing. The paper, threads and tear-out are not individually resolved. The compact driver and two-stud lifting handle are workcell adapters. Mesh and finishing compound are applied after this operation.
scores: Dream-1: 0 in 2,400 actions (120 s). Scripted demonstration: 1.0 in 2,400 actions (120 s).
